detail.longDescription: I think more websites/web applications should default to whatever the user's sans-serif, serif or monospace font is instead of deploying your custom fonts. To be clear, some legacy browsers cannot handle emojis well end this will need to be accounted for with custom fonts. However, I generally do not believe that the user's font is already the best pick because of multiple factors. Firstly, it saves space on your web application. You do not need to install a library in NPM that fetches from Google Fonts or install the fonts statically on your own web application. The default sans-serif font exists and is likely good enough for your use case. The conclusion is that you could set your font family to use that instead and save space for your project. Secondly, it helps for accessibility and doesn't force the user to override your CSS just to account for something like dyslexia, bad vision or other conditions. Your font probably looks nice to everyone who uses your app, if they even care, however it significantly disadvantages those who need fonts tailored to work around their condition. Generally, accessibility should be accounted for every case which is why we should aim to improve that for everything. To conclude, you will be helping accessibility on the web if you just use the users font instead of your own. Thirdly, the user may very well just want every application to use the same font. This isn't a problem and they should be able to do that, and if it means installing third-party extensions to modify the CSS of your website, they will do that. The question then becomes "why should we make it harder for people to choose how our page wants to look?", which the easy solution would likely be to not. Sure, you can probably say "to keep the style consistent" but it's already consistent for everyone because it's their font. Therefore, I do not consider it's worth trying to provide your own font. That last point basically sums up what I believe. Why make it difficult for the user, who may have their own reasons behind their choice of font, to forcefully override what you have set to something that works for them? You can just make your font sans-serif and get by with your day anyway, there's almost no reason to do that. I'm open for discussion for this issue, so if you have any arguments against it, I'm all for it. # webdev # programming # web # software # webdesign
